verdict.root_cause: At 20:29:14Z platform-automation applied an environment/config update to shippingservice that set QUOTE_SERVICE_ADDR — previously unset — to an address naming a decommissioned/non-existent quote backend (tr_8eb4ad4bdd98). Roughly three minutes later checkout began failing. Every failing trace stamps the error on checkoutservice's client span for ShippingService/GetQuote and on nothing else; cart/Redis, productcatalog/featureflag and currency edges are all clean, and the trace aborts before any later checkout stage (tr_a391b01a5a02). Shippingservice itself never errors: it keeps accepting well-formed GetQuote requests but stops emitting the quote-response line carrying an amount that accompanied every request earlier in the window (tr_c10985a9dc78), and its server span returns success in ~2ms. The consistent reading is that shippingservice, now pointed at a quote backend that does not exist, silently produces an empty/invalid quote and returns it as a nominal success; checkoutservice rejects that response at its client boundary and aborts the order before payment, email or fulfilment — matching checkout logs where order-placement start lines continue with none of the completion lines that followed them at 20:22 (tr_02e778da6175). The wrong address value is itself the failure mechanism: it is fast, not slow (no span exceeds ~4ms end to end), and no artifact or image changed anywhere (tr_8eb4ad4bdd98, tr_0fc36111a604, tr_f25e4e507bbf, tr_79f505a13285).
verdict.reasoning: Three independent lines converge on the same edge. Traces localise the error to exactly one boundary — checkoutservice's client span for ShippingService/GetQuote — with all other measured downstream edges healthy and no later checkout stage reached (tr_a391b01a5a02). Shipping logs show the behavioural change on that same path: identical, well-formed inbound requests, but the response-side quote amount line disappears, with no WARN/ERROR/crash lines, so the degradation is silent output corruption rather than a crash or refusal (tr_c10985a9dc78). Change history supplies the only mutation in the system in the onset window and it is on precisely that path: a newly introduced QUOTE_SERVICE_ADDR pointing at a host that appears decommissioned (tr_8eb4ad4bdd98). Change queries for checkoutservice and productcatalogservice are empty for the alert window, removing the competing deploy/flag hypotheses on the caller side (tr_0fc36111a604, tr_f25e4e507bbf, tr_79f505a13285). The class is bad_config rather than dependency_latency because there is no waiting anywhere — failing roots complete in single-digit-to-low-teens milliseconds with no span over ~4ms (tr_a391b01a5a02); it is not bad_deploy because no image or version entry exists, only an environment variable (tr_8eb4ad4bdd98); it is not resource_exhaustion because the process stays up, logs continuously, and most calls still succeed (tr_02e778da6175, tr_62e1cffccb80). The remedy is to restore QUOTE_SERVICE_ADDR to its prior unset state (or point it at a live backend), not to roll back an artifact — no artifact moved. Note the corpus pattern here: as in cart-redis-misconfig and cart-bad-image-tag, the culprit service reports clean error rates and clean spans while its caller carries all the errors, so a service-level error-rate reading would again have exonerated the wrong service.
open_questions: Mechanism inside shippingservice is inferred, not observed: its outbound HTTP client span completes successfully in ~2ms, which is not what a call to a genuinely unresolvable host normally looks like. Whether the quote failure is swallowed and converted to an empty/zero response, or the outbound span belongs to a different call entirely, was never established.
The ~3-minute gap between the 20:29:14 config apply and 20:32 onset is unexplained — pod rollout, env reload cadence, or cache expiry are all untested.

Exact onset is unpinned: both checkout and shipping log results are truncated, discarding roughly 20:22–20:33 in each (tr_02e778da6175, tr_c10985a9dc78). No error-filtered query was run over that middle interval.

Metrics show an intermittent 0–30% error ratio (tr_62e1cffccb80) while every sampled trace shows an identical deterministic failure shape (tr_a391b01a5a02). Whether the surviving 70% take a different path (cached quote, retry, different item set) is unresolved and matters for whether a revert alone is sufficient.
Triage crossed 4 unmeasured edges; no specialist covered cartservice change history or the other synchronous dependencies' change logs, so a second concurrent config push cannot be formally excluded.
The 18:32–20:22 lookback for checkoutservice was never executed — both change dispatches ran the same 15-minute window (tr_0fc36111a604, tr_f25e4e507bbf).

Whether reverting the variable takes effect without restarting shippingservice pods (env vars are typically read at process start) is unverified and determines whether config_revert alone restores service.
